bug_semantics: The interactive OIDC/OAuth authorization-code flow generates a random CSRF `state`, includes it on the authorization request, then accepts the IdP callback's `code` without comparing the returned `state` to the session value. An attacker who can complete a parallel auth request and deliver that callback (MITM / CSRF of the localhost redirect) can cause sigstore-python to exchange the attacker's authorization code, so the user signs under an attacker-controlled identity. The missing check is in `Issuer.identity_token()` (`code = server.auth_response["code"][0]` with no `state` compare); `_OAuthSession` only stores and sends `state`.
flaw_origin: First written in PR #56 member 37fa700a95d667fb9485c3284085402c0e5b4078 (`oidc: Support OAuth flow for signing`) by Alex Cameron. That commit added `RedirectServer.auth_request_params()` (`self.state = str(uuid.uuid4())` and `"state": self.state`) and `get_identity_token()` which parsed `server.auth_response["code"]` after only an `error` check. Parent 0fc52e3345e758db6119577fca05a75fa79f44c6 has JWT `Identity` parsing only—no OAuth server, no `state`, no callback. Later refactors (squash f785f90, file split, `OAuthSession` extraction, move of `identity_token` into `sigstore/oidc.py`) carried the same missing compare until 5e77497.
